## Proof

Let $f(X) = \log\det(X^{-1})$ defined on the cone $\mathbf{S}_{++}^n$ of $n\times n$ symmetric positive definite matrices, with $f = +\infty$ outside this cone. Since $X^{-1}\succ 0$, we have $\det(X^{-1})>0$, and
$$f(X) = \log\det(X^{-1}) = -\log\det X.$$

The Fenchel conjugate (with the inner product $\langle Y, X\rangle = \mathbf{tr}(YX)$ on symmetric matrices) is
$$f^*(Y) = \sup_{X\succ 0}\big\{\mathbf{tr}(YX) - f(X)\big\} = \sup_{X\succ 0}\big\{\mathbf{tr}(YX) + \log\det X\big\}.$$

Define $g(X) = \mathbf{tr}(YX) + \log\det X$ on $\mathbf{S}_{++}^n$.

**Case 1: $Y$ is not negative definite.** Then there exists a unit vector $v$ with $v^\top Y v \ge 0$. Take $X = t\, vv^\top + \varepsilon I$ with $\varepsilon>0$ fixed and $t\to\infty$; this stays in $\mathbf{S}_{++}^n$. Then
$$\mathbf{tr}(YX) = t\, v^\top Y v + \varepsilon\,\mathbf{tr}(Y) \ge t\, v^\top Y v + O(1),$$
which grows at least linearly in $t$ (when $v^\top Yv>0$) or is bounded below (when $v^\top Yv = 0$, perturb $v$ slightly to get strict positivity since $Y\not\prec 0$). Meanwhile $\log\det X = \log\det(\varepsilon I + t\,vv^\top) = \log\big(\varepsilon^{n-1}(\varepsilon+t)\big) = O(\log t)$. Hence $g(X)\to +\infty$, so
$$f^*(Y) = +\infty \quad\text{when } Y\not\prec 0.$$

**Case 2: $Y \prec 0$ (negative definite).** We maximize $g$ over $\mathbf{S}_{++}^n$. The differential is
$$dg = \mathbf{tr}(Y\, dX) + \mathbf{tr}(X^{-1}\, dX) = \mathbf{tr}\big((Y + X^{-1})\, dX\big).$$
Setting the gradient to zero gives the stationarity condition
$$Y + X^{-1} = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad X^{-1} = -Y \quad\Longrightarrow\quad X = -Y^{-1}.$$
Since $Y\prec 0$, we have $-Y\succ 0$, hence $-Y^{-1}\succ 0$, so the critical point $X^\star = -Y^{-1}$ is feasible.

To confirm it is a maximum: $\mathbf{tr}(YX)$ is linear in $X$, and $\log\det X$ is strictly concave on $\mathbf{S}_{++}^n$ (its Hessian $-X^{-1}\otimes X^{-1}$ is negative definite). Therefore $g$ is strictly concave, and the stationary point is the unique global maximizer. (Existence of the maximizer also follows because $g(X)\to -\infty$ as $X$ approaches the boundary of $\mathbf{S}_{++}^n$ or $\|X\|\to\infty$ when $Y\prec 0$.)

Evaluating at $X^\star = -Y^{-1}$:
$$g(X^\star) = \mathbf{tr}\!\big(Y(-Y^{-1})\big) + \log\det(-Y^{-1}) = \mathbf{tr}(-I_n) + \log\det(-Y^{-1}).$$
Using $\mathbf{tr}(-I_n) = -n$ and $\log\det(-Y^{-1}) = -\log\det(-Y)$,
$$f^*(Y) = -n - \log\det(-Y) = \log\det\!\big((-Y)^{-1}\big) - n.$$

**Conclusion.** The conjugate function of $f(X)=\log\det(X^{-1})$ is

$$\boxed{\,f^*(Y) = -n - \log\det(-Y) = \log\det\!\big((-Y)^{-1}\big) - n,\quad Y\prec 0,\,}$$

and $f^*(Y)=+\infty$ for $Y\not\prec 0$ (i.e., for $Y$ not negative definite). The effective domain of $f^*$ is the negative definite cone $-\mathbf{S}_{++}^n$.
